source_text:
In sanctum Antonium (homilia 8)
Τοῦ μακαριωτάτου Ἡσυχίου, πρεσβυτέρου Ἱεροσολύμων, ἐγκώμιον εἰς
τὸν ὅσιον πατέρα ἡμῶν Ἀντώνιον.
1 ∆ικαίων μνήμῃ καὶ ὁ κόσμος ἀγάλλεται, δικαίων μνήμῃ καὶ ὁ κόσμος
φωτίζεται, δικαίων μνήμῃ καὶ ἡ ἀνθρωπότης σκιρτᾷ, δικαίων μνήμῃ καὶ πᾶς τις
ἀκούων ἀγάλλεται. Νῦν Ἀντώνιος μνημονεύεται καὶ πάντες τῇ μνήμῃ φωτιζόμεθα,
Ἀντώ νιος ὁ τῶν οὐρανῶν πολίτης, ὁ πάσης ἀρετῆς καθηγητής, ὁ τοὺς ἀσάρκους ἐν
σαρκὶ μιμησάμενος, ὁ τῶν ἐκκλησιῶν λύχνος, ὁ τῶν ἱερέων παιδοτρίβης, τὸ τῆς
παρθενίας ἄνθος, τὸ τῆς ἁγνείας ἀπαύ γασμα, τῶν ἐν «ὄρεσι καὶ σπηλαίοις» ὁ
στέφανος, τὸ τῆς καρ τερίας ὑπόδειγμα, ὁ τῆς ἐγκρατείας ἐργάτης, ὁ ἀήττητος
πύκτης, τῶν προφητῶν ἡ στήλη, τῶν ἀποστόλων τὸ ἔσοπτρον, ὁ μετὰ θεοῦ καὶ
ἀνθρώπων δυνατός, ὁ μηδὲν ἐπὶ γῆς ἔχων, ὅλος δὲ εἰς οὐρανὸν ὁρῶν, ἄνω τοὺς
ὀφθαλμοὺς τείνων καὶ πρὸς ἐκεῖνο τὸ βραβεῖον τὸν δρόμον ἐπειγόμενος.
2 Ὁ πιστὸς ὡς Ἀβραάμ, ὡς ὁ Ἰσαὰκ εὐπειθής, καρτερικὸςὡς ὁ Ἰακώβ, ὡς
Ἰωσὴφ σιτοδοτῶν τὴν Αἴγυπτον, θαυμάτων παντοδαπῶν ὡς Μωυσῆς ἡνιοχῶν τῇ
διδασκαλίᾳ, ἔψαλλεν ὡς ∆αυὶδ καὶ τοὺς δαίμονας ἤλαυνε, ναὸν ἑαυτὸν μείζονα τῷ
θεῷ προσήγαγεν, ὡς ∆ανιὴλ ἐπέταττε τοῖς λέουσιν, ὡς ὁ Βαπτιστὴς ἐκκλησιάζει τὴν
ἔρημον, ὡς ὁ Θεολόγος «ἐπὶ τὸ στῆθος τοῦ Ἰη σοῦ» διὰ τῆς εὐαγγελικῆς μελέτης
«ἀνακείμενος», «καθ' ἡμέ ραν» ὡς Παῦλος «ἀπέθνῃσκεν».
3 Ἀλλὰ γὰρ καὶ ἡμεῖς ἀντλοῦμεν καὶ ἡ ληνὸς ὑπερβλύζει, οἱ πίθοι γέμουσιν,
«ὑπερχεῖται τὰ ὑπολήνια»· ὅσον τρέχομεν, μεῖζον τὸ στάδιον γίνεται· ὅσον ὁ πλοῦς
ἀνύεται, τοσοῦτον τῆς θαλάσσης δηλοῦται τὸ ἀμέτρητον. ∆εῦρο τοίνυν καὶ ἡμεῖς τὰ
τοῦ Παύλου εἴπωμεν· «Ἐπιλείψει με διηγούμενον ὁ χρόνος ἐπὶ Γεδεών, Βαράκ,
Σαμψών, Ἰεφθάε, ∆αυίδ τε καὶ Σα μουὴλ καὶ τῶν προφητῶν»· τούτους γὰρ ἐν αὑτῷ ὁ
πατὴρ τῶν συγκροτουμένων θεάτρων ἀνέλαβε· πολλῶν γὰρ χρεία ῥημάτων καὶ
ὁδηγὸς ἐγὼ τοῖς πράγμασιν, ἐπειδὴ κάμνει ὁ λόγος τὸ ἔργον ἐξηγούμενος. Ἕτερον
σκιᾶς χαρακτήρ, ἕτερον ἀληθείας ἐνέρ γεια. Ἄλλο εἰκὼν καὶ ἄλλο τοῦτο οὗπερ
εἰκὼν τυγχάνει τὸ δει κνυόμενον· εἰκονίζουσιν οἱ λόγοι τὸ ἔργον, ἀλλ' οὐχ οὕτως ἡ
orientation: Hesychius opens his encomium at Antony's feast, declaring that the commemoration of the righteous enlightens the world before listing Antony in a chain of biblical figures.
pass_a_gloss: Encomium by the most blessed Hesychius, priest of Jerusalem, to our holy father Antony. By commemoration of the righteous even the world rejoices, and by commemoration of the righteous even the world is enlightened, and by commemoration of the righteous even humanity leaps, and by commemoration of the righteous even everyone who hears rejoices. Now Antony is commemorated and we all are enlightened by the commemoration, Antony the citizen of the heavens, the teacher of every virtue, the one who imitated the bodiless ones in flesh, the lamp of the churches, the trainer of the priests, the flower of virginity, the radiance of purity, the crown of those in "mountains and caves", the example of endurance, the worker of self-control, the undefeated boxer, the pillar of the prophets, the mirror of the apostles, the one strong with God and with men, the one having nothing on earth but wholly looking to heaven, stretching the eyes upward and hastening the race toward that prize. Faithful as Abraham, obedient as Isaac, enduring as Jacob, giving grain to Egypt as Joseph, driving all kinds of wonders by his teaching as Moses, he sang psalms as David and drove out the demons, he brought himself near to God as a greater temple, commanding the lions as Daniel, making the desert into a church as the Baptist, reclining "on the breast of Jesus" through gospel meditation as the Theologian, "daily" dying as Paul. But indeed we also draw and the wine vat overflows, the jars are filled, "the vats overflow"; as much as we run, greater becomes the course; as much as the voyage is accomplished, so much of the immeasurable extent of the sea is shown. Come then let us also say the words of Paul: "Time will fail me telling of Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, and David and Samuel and the prophets"; for the father of the assembled contests took these up in himself; for there is need of many words and I am a guide in regard to the deeds, because speech grows weary explaining the work. Different is the imprint of shadow, different the working of truth. Different is an image and different is the thing shown which happens to be that of which it is an image; words depict the work, but not thus the [tongue ... breaks off].

choices.why: brief glossary requires commemoration for liturgical feast, not memory
theatron here is trials/contests in the Hebrews 10:33 sense embraced by monastic communities, not buildings; avoids opaque spectacles
paidotribes is athletic trainer, keeping boxer/wrestling imagery of the passage

choices.english: giving grain to Egypt as Joseph
choices.why: literal participle of supplying grain, avoids hyphenated compound

bible_refs.note: Ἐπιλείψει με διηγούμενον ὁ χρόνος ἐπὶ Γεδεών, Βαράκ, Σαμψών, Ἰεφθάε, ∆αυίδ τε καὶ Σαμουὴλ καὶ τῶν προφητῶν
ἐπὶ τὸ στῆθος τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἀνακείμενος

pass_b_english: An encomium of the most blessed Hesychius, presbyter of Jerusalem, on our holy father Antony.

The commemoration of the righteous makes the world rejoice. The commemoration of the righteous gives the world light. The commemoration of the righteous makes humanity leap for joy. Everyone who hears rejoices in the commemoration of the righteous. Now Antony is commemorated, and by his commemoration we are all enlightened.

Antony is a citizen of heaven and a teacher of every virtue. In the flesh he imitated those without flesh. He is the lamp of the churches and the trainer of the priests. He is the flower of virginity and the radiance of purity. He is the crown of those in mountains and caves (Hebrews 11:38) and the model of endurance. He is a worker of self-control and an undefeated boxer. He is the pillar of the prophets and the mirror of the apostles. He is strong with God and with people. He holds nothing on earth but looks wholly toward heaven. He lifts his eyes on high and hurries his race toward that prize.

He was faithful as Abraham and obedient as Isaac, enduring as Jacob. Giving grain to Egypt as Joseph, he guided wonders of every kind by his teaching as Moses did. He sang as David did and drove out demons. He offered himself to God as a greater temple. As Daniel did, he gave commands to lions. As John the Baptist does, he gathers the desert into a congregation. As John the Theologian, through meditation on the Gospel he reclines on the breast of Jesus (John 21:20). As Paul does, he died daily (1 Corinthians 15:31).

We too draw, yet the winepress overflows. The jars fill and the vats run over (Joel 3:13 / 4:13 LXX). The more we run, the longer the course becomes. The more the voyage advances, the more the boundlessness of the sea is revealed. Come then, let us also speak the words of Paul: "Time will fail me as I tell of Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David and Samuel and the prophets" (Hebrews 11:32). For Antony, the father of the assembled contests, took all these figures up into himself. Many words are needed, and I serve as a guide to the deeds, since speech grows weary in setting forth the work. The imprint of a shadow is one thing, the working of truth another. An image is one thing, and what the image displays is another. Words portray the deed, but not in the same way does the...
notes: source has line-break spacings: Ἀντώ νιος, ἀπαύ γασμα, καρ τερίας, Ἰη σοῦ, ἡμέ ραν, Σα μουὴλ, ἐνέρ γεια; read as single words
final clause breaks off at ἀλλ᾽ οὐχ οὕτως ἡ and continues in next section; glossed what is there without completing it

problems.why: Joel 2:24 speaks of winepresses overflowing with wine and oil; the exact quoted phrase comes from Joel 3:13 (4:13 LXX).
problems.ruling: Source quotes «ὑπερχεῖται τὰ ὑπολήνια»; English cites Joel 2:24, not the verse of that exact phrase.

fixed: wrong_scripture: fixed Joel 2:24 to Joel 3:13 / 4:13 LXX — source «ὑπερχεῖται τὰ ὑπολήνια» is the exact wording of Joel 4:13 LXX (= Joel 3:13 in modern English), not Joel 2:24.

problems.source_quote:

problems.why: The entire Greek superscription naming the author (Hesychius, presbyter of Jerusalem), the genre (encomium), and the subject (our holy father Antony) is omitted.
problems.fix: An encomium of the most blessed Hesychius, presbyter of Jerusalem, on our holy father Antony. The commemoration of the righteous
problems.ruling: Superscription Τοῦ μακαριωτάτου Ἡσυχίου… Ἀντώνιον is absent; author, genre, and subject framing are lost.

problems.quote: Words portray the deed, but not in the same way.
problems.source_quote: εἰκονίζουσιν οἱ λόγοι τὸ ἔργον, ἀλλ' οὐχ οὕτως ἡ
problems.why: The Greek breaks off mid-clause at the article ἡ; rendering it as a finished sentence ('not in the same way') drops ἡ and invents a closed meaning.
problems.fix: Words portray the deed, but not in this way does the...
problems.ruling: Source breaks at ἀλλ' οὐχ οὕτως ἡ; English closes the clause and drops the unfinished ἡ phrase.

last_rejected.quote: he reclines on the breast of Jesus (John 21:20)
last_rejected.source_quote: ὡς ὁ Θεολόγος «ἐπὶ τὸ στῆθος τοῦ Ἰη σοῦ»
last_rejected.why: John 21:20 does not speak of reclining on Jesus' breast; that scene is John 13:23.
last_rejected.fix: through meditation on the Gospel he reclines on the breast of Jesus (John 13:23).
last_rejected.ruling: John 21:20 explicitly mentions leaning on Jesus' breast (ἐπὶ τὸ στῆθος); the Greek blends 13:23 (ἀνακείμενος) and 13:25/21:20, so 21:20 is not wrong.
